# Labor Cost Per Barrel {.project-hero-title}

**Role:** Lead Developer & Analyst
· **Organization:** Select Water Solutions
· **Status:** Built — Aug 2026

::: {.project-hero-tags}

## The Problem {.project-section-heading}

Labor cost per barrel was being served by a single Power BI measure that
assembled an entire client-side JavaScript dashboard inside one DAX
string. It worked, but it was hard to test, hard to change, impossible to
version-control meaningfully, and tied to Power BI's rendering quirks.
Operations leaders wanted a faster, filterable view with drill-through to
the people and sites behind each number.


## The Solution {.project-section-heading}

I ported the dashboard to a server-rendered FastAPI + Jinja2 app on the
same platform as the rest of the reporting fleet, translating the
original shaping logic into SQL and pandas as written — port first, don't
"fix" anything mid-port — so the new app could be verified line for line
against the Power BI version.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 8
flowchart LR
    A[dbt model<br>load_labor_cost_per_bbl] --> B[Parameterized SQL<br>+ pandas shaping]
    B --> C[Ranked Site Table]
    B --> D[Single-Site Detail]
    C --> E[Drill-Through<br>to Employees]
    D --> E
    B --> F[CSV Export]
```

### Getting the grain right

The source table is not a clean date × site table. Open-month rows carry
one record per employee, while closed-month rows are site-level only —
and the barrel volume is a *site-level* figure repeated onto every
employee row. Summing it would multiply-count volume by headcount and
quietly deflate every cost-per-barrel number. The app aggregates volume
with `MAX` and labor cost with `SUM` at the site-and-day level, and the
test suite pins that behavior down.

### Filters and timeframes

Region, sub-region, and site are independent multi-select filters using
the platform's shared filter pattern. Timeframes cover month-to-date,
trailing twelve months, all-time, and — added after launch feedback — a
custom date range with graceful fallback when the range is unusable.
Every on-screen table has a matching CSV export that honors the same
filters.

### What Changed for the Business

- **Cost per barrel is traceable** — from a ranked site table down to the
  employees behind a site's number
- **Maintainable** — logic lives in version-controlled Python and SQL
  rather than inside a measure string
- **Consistent with the fleet** — same auth, health checks, filter UI,
  and export behavior as every other analytics app


## Technical Stack {.project-section-heading}

| Component | Technology | Purpose |
|:----------|:-----------|:--------|
| Backend | FastAPI, Jinja2 | Server-rendered pages and routes |
| Data Source | PostgreSQL, dbt | Cross-schema read from a governed dbt model |
| Shaping | pandas | Ports the original dashboard's rollup logic |
| Auth | Entra group membership | Same access model as sibling apps |
| Testing | pytest | Offline rendering tests with an in-memory query fake |
